text:
White House's official Rapid Response team denied the sleeping allegation(Image: Getty)

Fox News interrupted its scheduled programming during Donald Trump's press briefing in the Oval Office, as the US president seemed to be "dozing off", prompting viewers to mockingly dub him the "Commander-in-Sleep".

In a video shared on X, Trump was observed reclining in his chair as he yielded the floor to Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Lee Zeldin and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum.

Trump was spotted with his eyes shut for extended periods before turning toward Lee, who said, "For too long, you saw Democrats who were telling these coal miners they should just learn to code. And what we saw at the Biden administration at the EPA was regulation, after regulation, trying to strangulate its existence."

The incident drew considerable attention, with Democratic New York Governor Kathy Hochul's press office tweeting: "Sleeping is far better than listening to Lee Zeldin talk." This comes after the president's odd comment sparked concern following his 6-day disappeaance.

The White House rejected claims that Trump was asleep.

This isn't the first time the president has been captured "sleeping" on camera. In a comparable incident on May 11, a journalist posted a photograph of Trump with his eyes closed, reports the Express.

On that occasion, the team responded swiftly and dismissed the allegations of sleeping. They said: "His eyes are literally open in the clip you posted."

Donald Trump appeared to be nodding off during a press briefing(Image: Getty)

White House spokesperson David Ingle also addressed The Daily Beast's press inquiry: "President Trump is the sharpest, most accessible, and energetic president in American history," further stating, "President Trump is working around the clock to make our country greater than ever before."

Secretary of State Marco Rubio had previously pushed back against claims that Trump dozed off during Cabinet meetings and other public engagements.

During a congressional hearing, he declared: "That's false. I've never seen him fall asleep. On the contrary, the guy doesn't sleep, which is a big problem because he calls me at two in the morning. He calls me at five in the morning. And, you know, I like to sleep a little bit."
